Baron Virril

Overview

Baron Virril commands the Canian holdouts on Jigran against Firez’s Khadaganian forces. Proud of his family, he dislikes asking for aid even after losing Dar-Ulgorn. Kir’s arrival, the fight against the undead and the recruitment of powerful allies give his army a chance to attack Firez’s stronghold. He imagines a restored, prosperous Jigran ruled by his descendants. [1, 2, 3]

Return to Jigran and Dar-Leanos

The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where Baron Virril questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son Dartas and the overworked Master Stark. Stark provides a password for Uncle Rad, a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. [4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 8, 9]

Jaminin’s experiment and the undead

The trail of the local undead leads to Jaminin on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]

Dartas, Kel and the duel

Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. [17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22]

Weapons, Dartas and preparations for war

Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead, drawing on a book he read. Stark sends him to an abandoned forge rather than allow a youngster to work in his own smithy. When Kir returns with the alloy, Kel recognises the source of the craftsman’s resistance: a hereditary master is ashamed of learning something his father never taught him. Kir presents the discovery as knowledge Stark can pass to his own son. The smith agrees to try it, and the baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. The improved weapons strengthen his preparations for an offensive. [19, 23, 24, 25, 20, 26, 27]

The Joon cache and allies for the assault

The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. The cache is found in the valley Rad hopes to settle after the war. Dartas’s account of a nearby village destroyed by harpies points Kir to the rectangular amulet needed at its sealed entrance; Tui-Len supplies the remaining magical help. During the assault, Firez sends the city’s population, transformed into undead, against the Canian force. Kir must break through this army to reach the palace. [28, 29, 3, 30, 31, 26, 32, 33]
